text:
julia: Heads up — rolling maintenance for a firewall rule rollforward in us-east1 is hitting an anomaly. We're pausing the rest of the fleet drains and extending the window by ~30m. I'll outline the plan below.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: firewall-rollforward/us-east1 at 03:00 UTC. Status: started on 4476543210.

samir: What anomaly? packet drops, BGP, or control-plane auth?

julia: Packet filter mismatch on egress path to 10.0.0.0/8 from some racks — looks like a stale ACL slipped into the new ruleset. Observed increased connection resets to redis-proxies.

kevin: Can we hot-rollback the rule set? If we rollback, do we still need node drains?

julia: We're rolling back the new rule in the affected CIDR subset. Because some nodes already drained and rejoined with new iptables state, we need a short window to re-run prefix cache warmup and KV cache validation on those nodes. So drains paused; restart ETA +30m.

maria-se: Any customer-visible impact? Any Dedicated pools or Private installs affected? I need copy for SE notifications.

julia: No Dedicated pools were scheduled to be drained in the first wave, but a handful of Hosted edge racks in us-east1 got partially cycled. We saw ~1-2% increase in latency for streaming responses for a few minutes and a couple of transient 503s. Private deployments not touched.

nora: I can prepare a short customer note. Suggested wording: "Maintenance extended due to a network rule rollback; brief degradations observed, no data loss, full capacity to resume in ~30m." Want me to tag high-usage accounts?

maria-se: Yes tag the top 5 tenants in us-east1 and the three active trials — they care about latency. Also cc: solutions-eng to prep customers that run heavy streaming.

danny: Operational question: do we keep a warm spare pool running while we re-run warmup? Cost hit but reduces risk. How much spare do we need?

samir: If we keep 10% spare on padded pools we can backfill without impacting SLAs. That raises cost ~4-6% for the window.

danny: that's acceptable for a 30m extension. Approve to keep spares. :thumbsup:

julia: Plan: 1) rollback specific ACL block for 10.0.0.0/8 on affected edge racks (in progress). 2) mark nodes that rejoined as "prewarm-required" and run cache-warm script. 3) keep 10% spare prewarmed capacity in the pool. 4) resume drains in 30m with canary of 5 nodes, then ramp.

julia: Cache-warm command for ops runbook:
```
# mark node
redwoodctl node annotate node-abc prewarm=true
# kick warmup job
kubectl -n infra run warmup-$(date +%s) --image=infra-tooling:prod -- /bin/warm-prefix-cache --nodes node-abc,node-def
```

ops-bot: Action log: rollback applied by deploy-bot user at 4476543230. Net policy state verified on 12/14 targeted racks.

kevin: I'll run a canary resume in 10m and watch tail of streaming logs (/var/log/proxy/stream.log). Setting alert: egress-conn-resets > 5/min per rack -> pager.

samir: Also switch routing fallback to eu-north1 for best-effort heavy batches if latency climbs > 150ms for 5m. We have routing rules that can shift burst traffic.

julia: Good call. I'll flip the route policy to prefer eu-north1 for batching while preserving session affinity for in-flight chats.

nora: Draft customer note ready, short + links to status page. Will tag maria-se for review then send.

maria-se: Reviewed. Add: contact SE if you need an isolated Dedicated window.

oncall: Acknowledged — oncall monitoring ready. I'll post a final update when everything resumes.

julia: Thanks team. Will post another update at 4476543275 with final status.
